title: Functions Quiz 5
description: Every question has a trap: restrictions, order of composition, or a hidden swap.
instructions: Write maths answers with the keypad. Any equal form is accepted.
Every question has a trap. Slow down at the signs.

questions.question: Find $f^{-1}$ for $f(x)=3x-2$. One step is wrong. Tap it.
questions.explanation: $x=\dfrac{y+2}{3}$: divide by $3$, do not multiply. Watch out: undoing multiplication by $3$ is division.

questions.question: The domain of $f(g(x))$ with $f(x)=\dfrac1{x}$ and $g(x)=x-1$ excludes...
questions.explanation: $f(g(x))=\dfrac{1}{x-1}$, undefined at $x=1$. Watch out: $x=0$ is fine since $g(0)=-1$.

questions.question: If $f(x)=2x+1$ and $g(x)=x^{2}$, find $g(f(g(1)))$.
questions.explanation: $g(1)=1$, $f(1)=3$, $g(3)=9$. Watch out: work from the inside out.

questions.question: Find the domain of $\sqrt{4-x^{2}}$. One step is wrong. Tap it, then choose the correct step.
questions.explanation: $x^2\le4$ means $|x|\le2$, so $-2\le x\le2$. Watch out: $x=-5$ has $x^2=25>4$.

questions.question: If $f$ is even and one-to-one on its whole domain, it has an inverse.
questions.explanation: An even function has $f(-a)=f(a)$, so it cannot be one-to-one unless its domain is only $\{0\}$ or similar. Watch out: symmetry about the $y$-axis forces repeated outputs.

questions.question: Find $f^{-1}(x)$ for $f(x)=\dfrac{x+1}{x-2}$.
questions.explanation: $y(x-2)=x+1$ so $x(y-1)=2y+1$ and $x=\dfrac{2y+1}{y-1}$. Watch out: one sign slip in $-2y$ breaks the result.

questions.question: For $f(x)=x^{2}-4x+5$, find the minimum value of $f$.
questions.explanation: $x^2-4x+5=(x-2)^2+1\ge1$. Watch out: the minimum is $1$ at $x=2$, not at $x=0$.

questions.question: What is the range of $f(x)=x^{2}-4x+5$?
questions.explanation: Complete the square: $(x-2)^2+1\ge1$. Watch out: $f(0)=5$ is not the minimum.

questions.question: Which statements are **true**?
questions.explanation: The first three are standard facts. Watch out: $\ln 0$ is undefined and $f^{-1}$ is not a reciprocal.

questions.assertion: The function $f(x)=x^{2}$ has no inverse on all of $\mathbb R$.
questions.explanation: Both are true and the second explains the first: two inputs share one output, so $f$ is not one-to-one. Watch out: restricting to $x\ge0$ makes an inverse possible.

questions.question: $f(x)=\dfrac{x^{2}-1}{x-1}$ has domain all real $x$.
questions.explanation: At $x=1$ the denominator is $0$, so $x=1$ is excluded even though the fraction simplifies to $x+1$. Watch out: cancel only after finding the domain.
